text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Poland's trade deficit was $700 million in February and showed a decline by 200 percent compared with the record breaking level in January and was the lowest since July 1996, the National Bank of Poland (NBP), the cetnral bank said.

- The 1996 net profit of the KGHM copper conglomerate was 438.7 million zlotys showing a sharp decline compared with 972 million zlotys it netted the year before, the company's annual report said. The decline was caused by growing costs of production, falling copper prices worldwide and the need to create obligatory reserves, the auditors said.

- The Polish-Italian trade exchange deficit reached $2.4 billion in 1996, which was partly a consequence of Italy's discrimination against Polish businesspeople, who cannot form companies in Italy unless they hold residence permits. Poland's President Aleksander Kwasniewski has discussed the issue with Italian authorities during his current visit to Italy.
- The EU Industrial Commissioner Martin Bangemann will demand a timetable of Poland's telecommunications liberalisation during his visit to Warsaw to start today, the EU Commission said.

- Poland remains a leader in market transformation reforms among the ex-communist states in central and eastern Europe and will keep on advancing in the next few years, two forecasts by Germany's Economic Reasearch Institute (IWH) in Halle and by the Deutsche Bank Research said.

- The Goplana confectionery maker in Poznan, controlled by the Nestle concern, sold 9,000 tonnes of chocolate worth 304 million zlotys last year giving it an 18.8 percent market share, a report by the AmerNielsen market research firm said.

- The Odratrans SA river shipping firm's net profit plunged to 26,200 zlotys last year from 1.4 million zlotys the year before. The sharp decline was caused by the late start in the shipping season in 1996, the company said.
- The TIM wholesale electrical engineering equipment trader in Wroclaw, Southwestern Poland, is planning a share listing on the Warsaw bourse's parallel market by the end of 1997.
- The state-owned PKO BP bank and Credit Suisse First Boston have agreed to underwrite a three-year bond issue of the Gdansk power and heating plant nominally worth 21.07 million zlotys.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI

- The recent introduction of anti-dumping duties on zinc imports from Poland by the EU will decrease the net profit of the Boleslaw non-ferrous metals smelter by $1 million, the plant's marketing director said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- The Mieszko confectionery maker in Raciborz, southern Poland, will start a public share offer of 1.5 million shares priced at 13 zlotys a share this week. Mieszko has a two percent share in Poland's confectionery market.
ZYCIE
- Around 23 insurance firms will promote the policy offers at a two-day Second Insurance Exchange in Warsaw starting tomorrow.
PARKIET

- The Star truck maker in Starachowice, southern Poland, is planning a closed B-series share issue of up to 15 million shares by the end of this year, the company said. The issue is meant to increase the plant's share capital up to 150 million zlotys.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
